root_idea.summary: A root oriented toward rising into view and coming forth, yielding meanings of arrival, delegated approach, precedence, and elevation.
root_idea.development: From coming forth or appearing prominently, the root develops into approaching an authority as a delegation, arriving before others, and rising above or becoming elevated.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested verbal noun وَفْد is a distinct lexical form meaning a delegation or deputation.

senses.definition: A delegation or deputation arriving before an honored authority; in the Quran, the God-fearing are gathered before the Merciful as a delegation.
senses.usage_conditions: Used collectively for a group arriving in a deputed or honored capacity. The Quranic occurrence is وَفْدًا in 19:85.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come to a ruler, governor, or other great person as an ambassador, envoy, or messenger; also to go forth to him to convey gifts or seek aid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I, commonly construed with عَلَيْهِ or إِلَيْهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To send someone to a ruler or governor as an envoy or messenger, including to convey gifts or seek assistance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV causative, construed with عَلَيْهِ or إِلَيْهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to come; to bring someone to oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in idiomatic or figurative constructions such as asking what brought someone and saying that God brought a person to the speaker.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To rise above, overtop, overlook, or overhang something; also to become elevated or to raise and elevate a thing, including raising the head or erecting the ears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV elevation usage, attested of a saddle, an animal's withers, an elevated object, and an animal raising its head and ears.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hasten or go quickly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV usage attested in poetry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strive to outstrip or outgo one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested of camels and birds competing in speed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ascend.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested of mountain-goats ascending a mountain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come together to someone as ambassadors or envoys.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form VI reciprocal or collective approach to an authority.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask or desire someone to come.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare, tentatively reported Form X usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To raise oneself and sit erect rather than sitting at ease.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form X elevation usage in the manner of sitting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An honorific designation for religious travelers—the warrior, pilgrim, or performer of ʿumrah—as the ambassadors or delegates of God.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative religious expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The upper part or crest of an elevated long tract of sand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A geographical noun applied to a prominent sand formation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Coming to a ruler, governor, or other great person as an ambassador, envoy, or messenger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Verbal noun of وَفَدَ; also used in the expression for having the honor of coming as an envoy to the Prophet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who comes before a ruler, governor, or other great person as an ambassador, envoy, or messenger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Active participle used substantively for an arriving envoy or messenger.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A party or company that comes to a country or town, approaches rulers for a visit, aid, benefit, conquest, or congratulation, or is chosen to interview great people; it may travel on foot or mounted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can denote an arriving delegation or company whether or not it is formally selected for an embassy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel or bird that precedes the others in speed or in coming to water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage for an animal leading its companions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Either of the two projecting parts of the cheeks involved in chewing, which sink with old age.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Usually used in the dual وَافِدَانِ for the two cheek prominences.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A journey, in the phrase هُمْ عَلَى أَوْفَادٍ, ‘they are on a journey.’
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed or conventional expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Prominent or elevated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied specifically in the cited usages to a camel's hump and to the pubes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Erecting oneself and sitting without ease.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active participle describing an erect, restless manner of sitting.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Pointer to Form IV without an independent definition.
Form IV sending as an envoy.
Raising the head and erecting the ears.
Contains person, delegation, and explicitly Quran-related company senses.

cautions: The historical Quran citation associated with the وَافِد discussion is not converted into a modern surah:ayah location; the attested Quranic وَفْد occurrence is independently located by QAC at 19:85.
